name: The Ginkgo of the Botanical Garden

location.address: Jardim Botânico da Madeira Eng.º Rui Vieira, Caminho do Meio, Funchal

access: Paid entry, €7.50 adult, open daily 09:00-18:00 (last admission 30 min before close)
transport: Bus 29, 30, 31 or 31A from central Funchal (~10 min, ~€2), or the Teleférico do Jardim Botânico cable car from Monte
verify_notes: Register entry ASMAC n.87/90 (island code FSMMGB01), the IFCN/VALCONMAC official inventory of Madeira's singular and monumental trees (Duarte Olim survey, undated but citing the 2018/2021 regional legal framework for monumental trees). Height 18.0m, maximum perimeter 1.62m (162cm), notable reason 'Tamanho' (size). No age reference given in the register ('Sem referência'); the garden itself opened to the public in 1960 but that is the garden's founding, not a documented planting date for this specific tree, so age stays undocumented per the bridge-claim rule. One large ginkgo is catalogued among the garden's collection of roughly 3000 species; second source is the garden's own official visitor-information page confirming the garden's continued public operation, hours and fee, not a tree-specific corroboration. Flagged because the second source verifies the site rather than the individual specimen; the register is otherwise a single official government source. Alive: garden is actively operating in 2026 per its own site.

name: The Cypress of Quinta Magnolia

location.address: Quinta Magnólia, Rua Dr. Pita, Funchal

transport: Central Funchal park, walkable from the Lido seafront area or a short bus/taxi ride from the city centre
verify_notes: Register entry ASMAC n.92 (island code FSMCL01). Height 29.5m, maximum perimeter 6.06m (606cm), notable reason 'Tamanho' (size), condition 'Bom' (good) with permanent technical monitoring. The register calls it one of the largest specimens of its species on the island, over 1m trunk diameter and 30m+ height being noted as exceptional for Cupressus lusitanica. No age reference in the register; locally known as 'cedro-das-barracas' because its young leader shoot was traditionally cut to thicken the crown into a shade bower. Second source (lifecooler.com, a Portuguese leisure/tourism listings site, and corroborated by visitmadeira.com and madeira-web.com) confirms Quinta Magnólia as a real, currently operating 40,000sqm public park with free entry 08:00-20:00, but does not name this specific tree, so flagged as site-level rather than tree-specific corroboration, same caveat as mdr_001. Alive: park is in active public use in 2026.

name: The Copper Beech of the Emperor's Garden

location.address: Quinta Jardins do Imperador, Beco do Pico, Monte, Funchal

access: Paid entry, around EUR 1 (often free on Sundays), open weekdays 09:30-17:30, Sundays and holidays 10:30-17:30
transport: Monte parish, reachable by the Monte cable car from Funchal plus a short walk, or bus toward Monte
verify_notes: Register entry ASMAC n.100 (island code FMFSp01). Height 36.0m, maximum perimeter 3.52m (352cm), notable reason 'Tamanho' (size), condition 'Bom' (good). No age reference in the register. The estate, formerly Quinta do Monte, is where the exiled Emperor Karl I of Austria-Hungary lived and died in 1922; the register's historical notes describe the quinta's history (a tree reportedly planted to mark Napoleon Bonaparte's passage into his own exile is mentioned for the estate generally, but NOT tied to this specific beech, so that anecdote is not repeated as this tree's origin, per the bridge-claim rule). Second source: TripAdvisor reviews and madeiralovers.com confirm the garden is real, open to paying visitors, with the stated hours and fee, corroborating the site but not the specific beech (same site-level caveat as mdr_001/002). Alive: garden operating and reviewed as of 2026.

name: The Douglas Fir of Queimadas
transport: By car from Funchal via Santana, roughly 1 hour to 1 hour 15 minutes driving; no practical public transport directly to the park
verify_notes: Register entry ASMAC n.97 (island code SSPM01). Height 39.0m, maximum perimeter 3.61m (361cm), notable reason 'Tamanho' (size), condition 'Bom' (good). No age reference in the register. Queimadas Forest Park is the well-known trailhead for PR9, the Levada do Caldeirao Verde walk, and sits inside Madeira's laurisilva UNESCO area; the register notes it as one of the most visited sites on the island. Second source (TripAdvisor plus AllTrails and visitmadeira.com) confirms the park is real, free, and actively visited in 2026, but describes the park generally rather than this specific Douglas fir, so flagged as site-level corroboration only, same caveat as the other register entries. Alive: park in active public use in 2026. This is a planted exotic conifer inside a native-forest park, included on the size/register merit alone, not as a laurisilva specimen.

name: The Witch Tree of Fanal

location.address: Fanal, Paul da Serra plateau, Ribeira da Janela, Porto Moniz (within the officially designated Nucleo de Tis - Fanal)

access: Free, public land inside the Madeira Natural Park, rated 'muito facil' (very easy) by the register; a short walk from the Fanal parking area, but there is no on-site signage naming or pointing to this specific tree
transport: By car only; roughly 1 hour to 1 hour 15 minutes' drive from Funchal via ER209, well over an hour round trip because Paul da Serra is mountain plateau driving, not a suburban hop
verify_notes: The til grove at Fanal is officially designated as 'Nucleo de Tis - Fanal' (ASMAC n.77, island code PMRJOF01, register coordinates 32.809278,-17.141472), a 20-hectare nucleus of Ocotea foetens inside the laurisilva UNESCO World Heritage area, documented with 8 trunk perimeters (2.28, 2.27, 1.43, 0.68, 1.59, 1.05, 1.54 and 1.47m) and age given only as 'centenas de anos' (hundreds of years), referenced as predating Madeira's 1419 settlement. That register entry alone would be a grove, not a collectible point (see leads/blocked note). However, one specific specimen within this nucleus is independently and repeatedly identified across multiple travel and photography sources as the 'Witch Tree' or 'arvore da bruxa': a single ancient til with a dramatically twisted, moss-hung trunk and limbs read as outstretched arms, treated as Fanal's single most photographed tree (mymodernmet.com, journeyera.com, beyondmadeira.com which has a page dedicated to this one tree, rexby.com). A community-contributed OpenStreetMap node (id 11893400096) independently tags this exact spot 'Witch tree' with denotation=natural_monument, roughly 350m from the register's stated nucleus coordinate, i.e. within the same grove area. Combining the official register (existence, species, protected status, rough age) with the independent OSM identification plus multiple independent travel/photography write-ups (identity, fame, appearance) clears the two-source bar for THIS specimen, distinct from the grove as a whole. Flagged and location_precision set to approximate rather than confirmed because sources explicitly warn there is no signage and visitors 'need to search and guess' to find it, so this pin should be read as 'this area of the grove', not a surveyed trunk position. Age_min/max is a broad band reflecting tourism-source claims of '500 to 600 years' against the register's vaguer 'hundreds of years'; treated as an estimate repeated no more precisely than the sources allow, not a derived calculation. Alive: multiple 2024-2026 travel and photography posts describe visiting it recently; Madeira's 2016 wildfire is known to have reached parts of the island's laurisilva but no source reports damage to this specific grove or tree.

name: The Dragon Tree Grove of Neves

location.address: Jardim do Nucleo dos Dragoeiros das Neves, Caminho da Portada, Sitio das Neves, Sao Goncalo, Funchal

access: Free entry, public garden with an information centre open Monday-Friday 09:00-12:30 and 14:00-17:30; guided visits available by contacting the centre
transport: About 5km from central Funchal by road; no direct public transport noted, taxi or car recommended
verify_notes: Register entry ASMAC n.86 (island code FSGDD01): 'Nucleo de Dragoeiros', height 13.0m, maximum perimeter 4.77m (477cm), age 'Sem referencia' but description calls the group 'um notavel grupo de dragoeiros centenarios' (a notable group of centenary dragon trees), so 'over a century' is repeated as vaguely as the register states it, not sharpened further. Purpose-built conservation garden acquired by the Regional Government of Madeira specifically to protect this group; unlike the Fanal til nucleus this is a compact, purpose-built, named garden (not a stretch of forest) with its own official IFCN information centre page confirming address, phone, opening hours and free access, independently corroborated by the tourism board (visitmadeira.com). Treated as ONE ensemble entry under the same rule that allows a compact famous grouping with one obvious place to stand (comparable to how this project treats other named grove/avenue ensembles): the garden itself, not any single trunk, is the destination, and it is signposted and staffed, unlike Fanal's informally-nicknamed specimen. Dragon trees are native to Madeira and the Canaries and slow-growing (roughly 10 years to reach 2-3m per IFCN), consistent with 'centenary' framing. Alive: information centre and garden actively described as operating in 2026 sources.
